newsitem.title: USA: US Sen. Lott says W.House pushing too far on taxes.
newsitem.headline: US Sen. Lott says W.House pushing too far on taxes.

text.p: Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott said Tuesday the White House was pushing too far on some tax issues in discussions related to the budget resolution which is expected to be considered by committees this week.

"Both sides are trying to ... clear up misunderstandings and I think that the administration is trying to push the envelope beyond what was agreed to by any stretch of the imagination," the Mississippi Republican said.
"We agreed to no limits on capital gains or estate tax, and we're not getting into that," Lott told reporters.

"Also we think it's important that we not allow spending to creep up through these negotiations and we're trying to get to an understanding so we can move the budget resolution through, I think we're going to be able to do that," Lott said.

The White House has indicated areas where it would like more spending than agreed to by Republicans, Lott said. Also, "there are areas where they would like to put some limits on how we do the tax cuts, and we're not going to agree to that," he added. But Lott said the problems would likely be resolved and the budget framework go before the committee this week.
The House Budget Committee said it will consider the budget resolution Wednesday, the Senate Budget Committee also expects to do so this week, but has not yet set the day.
A spokesman for the Office of Management and Budget said the White House was not trying to dictate to the Republicans how to do tax cuts outside of the priorities carved out by the administration.
The White House's top two tax priorities are a child tax credit and tax provisions related to higher education.
